dedupe_keys.name: clear collaborative petrochemical air pollution map

description: The Petrochemical Air Pollution Map visualises the multi-pollutant health risk that communities face from petrochemical facilities releasing toxic chemicals into the air, and the chemicals and facilities driving that risk. Users enter an address to see which chemicals and plants drive risk in their neighbourhood and how it compares with the rest of the country, filter the national view by priority chemicals such as ethylene oxide, and see facilities' compliance with environmental laws; the page cites Iberville Parish, Louisiana, with five plants releasing ethylene oxide. It is produced by Clear Collaborative, whose companion data directory was created by the Environmental Defense Fund, and it explains that EPA combines facility-reported pollution with other emissions data to estimate pollution. Coverage is the United States. The map is available free online under the site's terms of use. Caveats: risk estimates are modelled, not measured, as the page notes that air monitors often show different concentrations, and the underlying data sources and years are not detailed on the page read. For simulation it shows where people live near petrochemical plants with high chemical release risk, useful for exposure analysis and emergency planning around industrial accidents. It is related to the Life at the Fenceline chemical facility map record in this catalogue.
